name: Question 18
worked_solution:
First, we substitute $u={t}^{2}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=2t\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=t\text{d}t.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $t\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={t}^{2}$ is as follows:

| $t$ | $1$ | $-\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}\frac{6t}{{t}^{4}+3}\,\text{d}t=3{\int }_{\infty }^{1}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}u=-3{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{6t}{{t}^{4}+3}\,\text{d}t & =-3{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-3{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-3\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{u}{\sqrt{3}})]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})) \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}})]-\frac{\pi }{6})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}})]=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}})]=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/c870dd367332455f2d4c35f85a188c64385a5195ca1058405a93f84c4ce31fd1.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}\frac{6t}{{t}^{4}+3}\,\text{d}t & =-\sqrt{3}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}})]-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
